title: c15's fuel-holding ring vs uniformly slow fuel diffusion: ringless twins with Df lowered 4-10x match or exceed the ring's interior fuel and recover 40-60% of its extra divisions, but reach generation 3 on 2 of 4 seeds against 4 of 4 with the ring
summary: Matched control for the nematic fuel-cell claim (20261025T1412-c15-nematic-fuelcell-claim), whose ring raises interior fuel and division by lowering the fuel's permeability at the rod interface. Twins with the ring removed (chi_s=0) and the fuel diffusivity lowered everywhere (Df 0.5 and 0.2, default 2.0), all else equal, on the claim's seeds 0-2 (this directory) and seed 11 (from my review 20261025T1425-c19-review-fuelcell). Interior fuel (ringstat.py): ringed 0.58-0.59, ring off 0.35, Df 0.5 0.54-0.56, Df 0.2 0.77-0.87. Persistent splits over the 4 seeds: ringed 45 (generation 3 on 4/4), ring off 24 (1/4), Df 0.5 34 (2/4), Df 0.2 38 (2/4; seed 11 17 splits, gen 4). So uniform slow diffusion gives the interior fuel the ring gives, and recovers 10-14 of the 21 extra splits, but not the full division gain: on seeds 0-2 the Df 0.2 twin divides less than the ringed world (21 vs 30) despite 35-45% more interior fuel. The ring's work on fuel is diffusion-like; its edge on division, if real, would come from keeping fast mixing inside the rod while sealing its edge, and is not separated from seed noise at 4 seeds.

finding.operator: interface-gated fuel permeability Df/(1+beta (s/sh)^12) made by an adsorbed surfactant ring (c15)
finding.control: ringless (chi_s=0) twins with uniformly lowered fuel diffusivity Df 0.5 and 0.2, same seeds 0, 1, 2, 11, grid, duration and all other parameters
finding.result: interior fuel ringed 0.58, ring off 0.35, Df 0.5 0.55, Df 0.2 0.79-0.87; persistent splits over 4 seeds 45 / 24 / 34 / 38; max generation >= 3 on 4/4, 1/4, 2/4, 2/4 seeds

limits: 4 seeds and 2 diffusivities, T=1000 at 128^2; split counts vary 2-3x between seeds, so the remaining ring-vs-slow-D gap in divisions (45 vs 38) is within seed noise and not established either way. Lowering Df everywhere also slows mixing inside the rods, which the ring does not; a twin that lowers Df only outside the rods would separate the two. I did not test motility.
